messages:
alex_customer: Hey team — running into a weird embeddings error after migrating to our new client. Previously we got 1536-d vectors from text-embedding-3-large; now calls return a 512-d vector and downstream math breaks.

Sample response: 
```\n400 Bad Request\n{\n  \"error\": \"Embedding dimension mismatch: model 'text-embedding-3-large' expects 1536 dims but got 512\"\n}\n```\n\nI can reproduce locally and in prod. Request id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3. Sending a single item per request. Any ideas? urgent, this is breaking search indexing.

maya_support: Thanks for the report, alex — sorry for the trouble. Can you paste the exact request body + headers you used (curl or SDK snippet)? Also which SDK and version?

alex_customer: Using our in-house wrapper around requests (python) but here's the exact curl I used to replicate:

```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \\\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":"[\"Why is my vec short?\"]"}'\n```

maya_support: ahhh. can you try sending input as a JSON array rather than a stringified array? e.g. "input": ["Why is my vec short?"] not "input": "[\"...\"]".

irene_engineer: adding some context — the embeddings API accepts either a single string ("input": "hello") or a list of strings ("input": ["a","b"]) for batching. If you send a string that contains JSON (like "[\"hello\"]"), our parser treats that as a literal string, which can confuse client-side wrappers or light-weight routers that inspect types. In some cases our ingestion heuristics can misinterpret nested numeric arrays (e.g., [[0.1,0.2,...]]) as precomputed vectors, leading to a dimension validation path that expects the precomputed vector shape. That leads to the exact mismatch you're seeing.

alex_customer: oh that makes sense. We do a `json.dumps(body)` and then call `requests.post(url, data=payload)` because of older code. I guess requests.data doesn't set the JSON param so we're double-serializing?

irene_engineer: yep — double-serialization is the usual culprit. Two reproductions for triage:

1) Broken (what you have):
```\n# python-ish pseudo\npayload = json.dumps({"model": "text-embedding-3-large", "input": ["Why is my vec short?"]})\nrequests.post(url, headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"}, data=payload)\n# This ends up sending \"input\": \"[\\\"Why is my vec short?\\\"]\" on the wire\n```

2) Correct:
```\nrequests.post(url, json={"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["Why is my vec short?"]})\n# OR\nrequests.post(url, headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"}, data=json.dumps({"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["Why is my vec short?"]}))\n```

josh_prod: quick note about the server-side behavior that caused the confusing message: when the parser sees top-level arrays of numbers (e.g. [[0.1,0.2,...]]) we assume customer is sending precomputed numeric vectors for the embeddings-create-from-vector workflow and route to a different validation path that enforces exact dims for the model. If the payload is a string ("[1,2,3]") it can sometimes still hit that path after an intermediate component attempts to coerce types. We shouldn't return a 512-vs-1536 message for that case, but we do today — raising an internal followup to make the error clearer. filing: INC-embed-ux-239.

maya_support: For immediate unblock, could you try the correct curl and confirm? Also please include a failing request id if you have one.

alex_customer: tried the corrected curl and it works — embeddings are 1536 now. Example (trimmed):
```\nRequest: {"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["Why is my vec short?"]}\nResponse: {"data":[{"embedding":[0.01, -0.02, ..., 0.005],"index":0}],"model":"text-embedding-3-large"}\n```

alex_customer: Request id for broken run was rwd-req-0a1b2c3 (same as above). Confirming fixed on prod after we patched client to use `json=` param. :tada:

maya_support: awesome, thanks for verifying! We'll keep INC-embed-ux-239 for the server-side improvement (better error + detection for double-serialized JSON).

irene_engineer: followups and notes for the SDK/workaround: 1) validate input types before send (raise if you detect a string that looks like an array or starts with '[' and ends with ']'). 2) for numpy users, ensure `arr.tolist()` is used before json serializing. 3) for node clients, avoid `JSON.stringify` twice or passing the string to `body` instead of `json`.

josh_prod: pushing a small client-side validator to the official python SDK to detect obvious double-serialization and provide a helpful error. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/453 (will backport to 1.x).

maya_support: notes for support KB we should add: diagnostic checklist (headers, confirm content-type, verify `input` is not a JSON-string, sample curl). I'll add a paragraph and a copyable curl snippet.

alex_customer: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround. closing on our side.

deploy-bot: Deployed support KB update to /docs/support/embedding-input-shape.md (deploy id dpl-789).
summary: Customer reported embeddings returning wrong dimension; root cause double-serialized input (stringified array). Repro + fix provided; server follow-up filed; SDK validator PR created.
